func TestLegacyRollbackReturnFailureKeepsRecoveryProofAcrossPinChanges(t *testing.T) {
	f := newRolloutFixture(t)
	target := rolloutTarget("0.80.0")
	f.advance(target, "install")
	f.now = f.record().Deadline.Add(time.Second)
	f.advance(target, "rollback-check")
	record := f.record()
	record.RollbackRequired = nil
	if err := f.reconciler().Save(t.Context(), record); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	node := record.Node
	f.returnError[node] = errors.New("LB health check failed")
	f.now = record.Deadline.Add(time.Second)
	f.advance(target, "failed")
	if !f.drained[node] {
		t.Fatal("failed legacy return released the drain")
	}
	delete(f.returnError, node)
	status := f.statuses[node]
	status.ActionID = "" // Fresh healthy old status alone cannot prove rollback.
	f.statuses[node] = status
	before := len(f.effects)
	if err := f.tick(rolloutTarget("0.80.1")); err == nil || len(f.effects) != before || !f.drained[node] || f.record().ID != record.ID {
		t.Fatalf("legacy rollback return bypassed recovery proof: record=%+v effects=%v error=%v", f.record(), f.effects, err)
	}
}
roots.reason: Legacy rollback return failure retains the drain and original transaction after a target change without rollback acknowledgment; journal/status/effect assertions use only fixture JSON bytes, maps and hooks.

func TestRollbackAcknowledgmentWithAnErrorKeepsTheFence(t *testing.T) {
	f := newRolloutFixture(t)
	target := rolloutTarget("0.80.0")
	f.advance(target, "install")
	f.deferActions = true
	f.now = f.record().Deadline.Add(time.Second)
	f.advance(target, "rollback-check")
	node := f.record().Node
	status := f.statuses[node]
	status.ActionID, status.Error = CommandID(f.record().ID, "rollback"), "previous binary restart failed"
	f.statuses[node] = status
	if err := f.tick(target); err != nil || f.record().Phase != "rollback-check" || !f.drained[node] || slices.Contains(f.effects, "return:"+node) {
		t.Fatalf("errored rollback acknowledgment returned the node: record=%+v effects=%v error=%v", f.record(), f.effects, err)
	}
}
roots.reason: Error-bearing rollback acknowledgment keeps the fence; injected worker status and effect recorder are local.

rollout-fixture.scope: All callbacks including journal Load/Save, status, drain, health, return and send are fixture memory. Fresh Reconciler does not create a real restart/store boundary. Root-specific overrides are preserved in full assertion text.

rollout-state-machine.scope: Reconciler delegates all observations and external effects to callbacks; actual Tick path stops at synthetic fixture dependencies.

entity-identities.scope: ID generation/validation/derivation used for command and transaction identities; no assertion targets random entropy or a runtime boundary.

target-hash.scope: Deterministic JSON and SHA256 only; target construction provides local values.

context-dispatch.scope: Do clones request context and calls only the test-defined dispatcher; no real HTTP client invocation.

secrets-initializer.scope: Goroutine/select wrapper invokes an injected initializer blocked on a test channel. Real SDK initializer in readOCISecret is not called by this root.

pat-predicate.scope: Exported ValidAdminPAT delegates directly to local shape/length/ASCII predicate.

qualification_limits: No build/test/helper/scanner/parser/framework/formatter/probe/locks/privilege/cloud/signing/crypto/TerraBase execution or downloads. Ordinary file/Git/hash and metadata packaging only.
Fixture journal is serialized memory, not NATS/KV/filesystem/durable storage. Worker/daemon installation, rollback, mesh/application health and LB drain/return are not exercised.
Vault deadline/backoff tests replace actual transport/SDK initialization with local closures/channels; IMDS URL construction is not network access. PAT predicate proves shape only.
Safety/failure obligations are retained; no deletion/retirement/count/ledger/runtime/completion credit. Independent review required.
